newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria announces CA merger plans.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria announces CA merger plans.

text.p: Austrian market leader Bank Austria and recent acquisition Creditanstalt will merge their treasury, east European and investment banking activities, Bank Austria announced on Wednesday.

It had signalled it planned to bring the operations under one roof when it bought its former rival for some 17 billion schillings ($1.4 billion) in January. The details took shape at a meeting of the banks' joint management committee on Wednesday.
"Today the committee has taken some important decisions on implementing these first big integration projects," Bank Austria said in a statement.
It announced the two banks' commercial units in central and eastern Europe would merge, coming under a single holding company by the end of 1997.
"The aim is to achieve a unified identity on the markets in central and eastern Europe," the statement said.
A fusion of investment banking activities, currently split between Investmentbank Austria and Creditanstalt Investment Bank, would take place by September 30.

"This will ensure that we continue to build on our recognised strengths in central and eastern Europe," Bank Austria said. "The aim of the banking group is to shore up its position as number one in the region."
The group's future emphasis would be on corporate advisory and share trading, it continued.
Treasury operations would be combined with effect from 1998, Bank Austria added, thereby raising competitiveness and trading liquidity and improving the range of products offered.
-- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254 ($ = 12.27 Austrian Schillings)
